spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The first to be in grief is the primal wisdom of love. It is distressed because the goods and truths that proceed from it are held in oppression, having joined themselves to denial of good and to destructive falsity. They are confined under the full dominance of that ruling evil. Therefore wisdom remains in vigilant care over their state and is pained: whenever it perceives how suffering is being imposed on them, it is troubled and saddened for them.

The second to be troubled inwardly is the primary good that first confronts evil, whose full power and ordered domain are fixed in wisdom from the Divine. It too is troubled because the sufficient complement of its operative powers are placed in the midst of severe spiritual trial. For whenever it perceives them being harassed, it is continually aware of their lamentation as they cry out under the injuries inflicted by opposing evil and falsity that assail them without ceasing; and seeing this unremittingly, that primary good grieves and mourns for its powers.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the theme by showing grief as the vigilant pain of wisdom over oppressed goods and truths.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase rendered as “poison son” is unclear in form; taken functionally as destructive falsity arising from evil. “Watching over” translated as vigilant care.

paragraph_translations.notes: “Light-ship of his Father” resisted clean rendering; taken as being established within Divine wisdom as a containing and sustaining form. “Enemy” translated as opposing evil and falsity in active assault.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent and single-voiced: a two-step progression from wisdom grieving over oppressed derivations to primary good grieving over its operative powers under assault. Minor strain comes from damaged wording (“poison son,” “light-ship”), but their functions integrate smoothly into the same teaching.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: grief is taught by function (vigilant perception of the children’s affliction) and the narrative logic is continuous within the paragraph.
findings.evidence: The teaching arises from what the Mother DOES: she "grieves" because she is "[watching]tching over them" and "Whenever she might [see]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve." This is classic functional causality (perception → compassion/grief). The spiritual reading reports only a minor lexical stumble ("poison son" unclear) but notes it integrates functionally; that is a sign of damage/unclear word, not voice intrusion.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damaged/unclear lexeme rather than insertion: a corrupt or uncertain word-form forces interpretive smoothing, but it does not introduce a new administrative register or break the narrative.
findings.evidence: Text: "conjoined with the Darkness and the [poison]son." The spiritual reading explicitly flags: "The phrase rendered as 'poison son' is unclear in form; taken functionally as destructive falsity." This is the reader compensating for a textual crux. The sentence remains within the same affective-functional narrative (children afflicted by Darkness; Mother grieves), so excision would not improve coherence—only remove a real, if corrupt, object of conjunction.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate with minor local damage: grief is grounded in the First Man’s functional relation to his sons (he perceives their danger, hears their cries, sees their wounds). The only strain is an opaque image/term ("light ship"), not an administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Functional chain: "he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger"; "any time he may see" them troubled, "always he might hear the sound of their weeping"; "as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[grie]eve." This is correspondential causality (seeing/hearing suffering → grief). The spiritual reading’s stumble is confined to a phrase: "'Light-ship of his Father' resisted clean rendering"—a classic sign of difficult or damaged wording, not of a shift into jurisdictional listing or governance.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty (possibly idiom, loanword, or corrupt reading) that the reader paraphrases to preserve sense; not a seam-expansion or administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: "whose [greatness]ness and kingdom is established in the li[light] ship [of his Father]." The spiritual reading notes resistance and supplies a functional paraphrase ("established within Divine wisdom as a containing and sustaining form"). Importantly, the phrase is embedded in a descriptive clause and does not trigger a new mode (no named ranks, stations, authorities). Removing it would not resolve a narrative break; it would only delete a difficult epithet.

textual_criticism.summary: Four findings: two clean correspondential confirmations (¶2, ¶3) and two genuine-difficulty cruxes ("poison son" in ¶2; "light ship" in ¶3). No administrative-voice intrusions, no overlay blocks, and no seam-expansions are indicated by the spiritual reading; therefore no excision or annotation is recommended.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: ⟨p.147⟩ The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poison]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [watching]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [see]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.

⟨p.148⟩ [The]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [greatness]ness and kingdom is established in the li[light] ship [of his Father]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[grie]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (1–4) recommended none (no excision or annotation), including the difficult lexemes "[poison]son" (Finding 2) and "li[light] ship [of his Father]" (Finding 4), which were judged genuine difficulties rather than intrusive expansions.
